chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when brought the drinker of wine, would strike him. If he was brought again, he would strike him. If he was brought a third time, he would strike his neck (kill him). I asked: What about Nabidh? He said: When the drinker of Nabidh is caught and has become slightly intoxicated (intashaa), he is struck eighty times. I asked: What if he is caught a second time? He said: Strike him. I asked: And if he is caught a third time? He said: He is killed just as the drinker of wine is killed. I asked: What if the drinker of Nabidh is caught and has not become fully intoxicated? Is he flogged? He said: No.

key_terms.أَرَأَيْتَ: what do you think / I asked

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for drinking Nabidh if one is not fully intoxicated?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the gradation of punishment for Nabidh based on the degree of intoxication, distinguishing it from the fixed penalty for wine. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that eighty lashes apply only when the drinker exhibits clear signs of intoxication (intashaa), while a third offense results in execution, mirroring the ruling for wine. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the severity of the hudud is directly linked to the actual state of intoxication rather than mere consumption.
